hints.content:
First, note that the derivative of

$\displaystyle-2x-2x^2-\frac{{8}}{3}x^3-4x^4-...$

is

$\displaystyle-2-4x-8{{x}^{2}}-16{{x}^{3}}-...-2{(2x)}^{n-1}+...=-\frac{2}{1-2x}$

Then 

$\displaystyle\int{\left(-\frac{2}{1-2x}\right)dx}=\int{\left(-2-4x-8x^2-16x^3-...-2(2x)^{n-1}\right)dx}$

Using the $~u$-substitution $~u=1-2x~$ with $~du=-2dx\,$, we have

$\displaystyle\int{-\frac{2}{1-2x}}\text{ }dx=\ln \left( 1-2x \right)+C$

Therefore

$\displaystyle\ln(1-2x)+C=-2x-2x^2-\frac{8}{3}x^3-4x^4-...$

for some value of $~C\,$.

Now let $~x=0~$ and equate the right-hand sides of the last equation to see that $~C=0\,$.

Thus,

$\displaystyle -2x-2x^2-\frac{{8}}{3}x^3-4x^4-...=\ln \left( 1-2x \right)\,$

question.content:
We know that

$\displaystyle-\frac{2}{1-2x}=-2-4x-8{{x}^{2}}-16{{x}^{3}}-...-2{(2x)}^{n-1}+...$

for $x\in\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.

**Using this fact, find the function that corresponds to the following series.**

$\displaystyle -2x-2x^2-\frac{{8}}{3}x^3-4x^4-...$
